# AI/LLM Integration

Covers dimension 11. Sources referenced in [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Native AI Capabilities

### Universal AI Pieces

Activepieces provides "Universal AI pieces" — automations that use
admin-configured AI providers without requiring end users to authenticate
individually [19]:

| Property | Value | Source |
|----------|-------|--------|
| Default providers (cloud) | OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude) | [19] |
| Self-hosted | Admin configures providers, no credit limits | [19] |
| Cloud credits | 200 AI Credits included | [19] |
| First released piece | Text AI | [19] |
| Additional pieces | "More to be released" (no specifics) | [19] |

The admin-configured model means platform administrators set up API keys
centrally, and end users (or the PA) can use AI pieces without needing their own
API credentials [19]. For a self-hosted instance, the admin (you) configures the
providers once [19].

### AI Agent Capabilities

Discovery agents reported:
- Autonomous AI agents that make decisions and execute tasks (unverified)
- AI agents can use any of the 280+ pieces as tools via "Add Tool" (unverified)
- Dedicated AI Agents tab in the UI (unverified)
- AI copilot for step configuration and code generation [21]

These claims come primarily from marketing materials and third-party reviews and
could not be verified against official documentation in this research session.

### Supported AI Providers

From discovery and third-party sources [19][21][22]:
- OpenAI (GPT-4) — confirmed [19]
- Anthropic (Claude) — confirmed [19]
- Google Vertex AI, Google AI — reported (unverified)
- Other providers via Universal AI piece configuration — architecture supports
  it [19]

### Local LLM Support

No native Ollama integration [20]. GitHub issue #3307 requesting Ollama support
was still open during discovery. LocalAI integration reportedly exists but
details not confirmed.

## MCP (Model Context Protocol) Integration

Activepieces emphasizes MCP as a strategic differentiator [2][24]:

| Property | Value | Source |
|----------|-------|--------|
| MCP servers | 280+ pieces exposed as MCP; ~400 total servers claimed | [2] |
| Mechanism | All pieces auto-exposed as MCP servers | [24] |
| Compatible clients | Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf | [24] |
| Self-described as | "Largest open source MCP toolkit" | [2] |

Every Activepieces integration (piece) automatically becomes available as an MCP
server [24]. The GitHub repo claims "~400 MCP servers" while documentation cites
"280+ pieces as MCP" [2] — the discrepancy likely reflects that some MCP servers
bundle multiple tools from a single piece, or the count includes planned/beta
servers. The exact reconciliation is unclear from available sources.

**For the PA use case:** The PA could use MCP to discover and invoke Activepieces
workflows as tools, or Activepieces could expose its integrations as MCP servers
for the PA to call directly. However, the PA currently uses `claude -p`
subprocesses, not MCP-based tool discovery.

## Comparison to n8n AI Capabilities

| Capability | Activepieces | n8n |
|-----------|-------------|-----|
| LLM providers | OpenAI, Anthropic (confirmed) | 11 providers via LangChain |
| AI framework | Native pieces | LangChain integration (70+ nodes) |
| MCP support | ~280-400 servers | Bidirectional (client + server) |
| Vector stores | Not confirmed | 12 backends |
| Memory | Not confirmed | 8 backends |
| Agent architecture | Universal AI pieces, AI agents tab | Tools Agent (consolidated) |
| AI templates | Not confirmed | 6,137 AI-specific templates |

n8n's AI integration is more mature and comprehensive, with deep LangChain
integration, 70+ dedicated AI nodes, 12 vector stores, and 8 memory backends.
Activepieces' AI integration is newer and less documented, but the MCP approach
(exposing all integrations as MCP servers) is architecturally distinctive.

---

## Assessment for Personal Assistant Use Case

**Not a requirement, but a nice-to-have.** The PA is the LLM layer — the
workflow engine runs deterministic pipelines. Activepieces' AI integration adds
value primarily through:

1. **MCP servers:** If the PA evolves to use MCP tool discovery, Activepieces
   could expose its integrations as discoverable tools
2. **AI copilot:** Faster workflow creation when building new automations
3. **Universal AI pieces:** Simple "call an LLM" steps without managing API keys
   per workflow

For the current architecture (PA triggers workflows via webhook/API), the AI
integration is not a differentiator.
